related_resources.reason: Analyzes how late nineteenth-century Lunda, Chokwe, Imbangala, Luba and Portuguese informants assembled the Lueji-Chibinda Ilunga legend; not direct proof of a founding marriage.
Origins, dynastic authority by about 1700, Luba/Ruund distinctions, positional succession, perpetual kinship. Early causes are proposed mechanisms, not established institutions.
Seventeenth-century political context, mythic Kalala Ilunga, sacred kingship and councils, female ancestor iconography, dated examples of surviving material arts.
Challenges literal use of savanna origin stories in the absence of pre-nineteenth century written anchors. Full article beyond publisher extract not reviewed.
Pages 1-7: Upemba graves, Kisalian, Kabambian, copper cross ingots and later Luba material continuity. Graves do not directly document households or the dates of royal dynasties.
Supplementary orientation only; not a primary or sole historical authority.
